briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome. We will now begin the daily briefing by the Climate Change Spokesperson on October 27, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Increasing Warnings
sections.content: Global greenhouse gas concentrations have once again reached record highs, with South Korea's concentrations notably exceeding the global average [15, 24, 26, 36, 39, 40]. The most significant increase was observed in sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆), a gas with an atmospheric lifetime of 1,000 years, raising serious concerns [29, 41]. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) projects that greenhouse gas levels will reach an all-time high in 2025, warning of further intensification of global warming [155]. This situation has halted the progression of the next ice age, which had already begun [14], and suggests that we are moving further away from the Paris Agreement climate goals [148]. Domestically, 'climate crisis clocks' have been installed to urge the practice of carbon neutrality and raise public awareness [16, 17, 28, 33].

sections.title: ⚠️ Increasing Climate Change Impacts and Vulnerabilities Domestically and Internationally
sections.content: The direct impacts of climate change are widespread, both domestically and internationally. In South Korea, heatwaves and droughts, unseen for 100 years, have become commonplace. A vicious cycle where drought exacerbates heatwaves, which in turn cause more droughts, is rapidly altering grassland climates [3, 22]. Climate change is intensifying ecological disturbances, leading to phenomena like 'premature leaf fall' where leaves drop before autumn colors appear, and a 36% increase in pine wilt disease [4, 7, 10, 20]. Warnings have also been issued about an increased risk of spontaneous combustion, where fires ignite without an ignition source [13]. Internationally, climate change is contributing to new types of landslides [141], and in New York City, humid and hot summers have led to an increase in West Nile virus infections [146]. The reality of the climate crisis is manifesting globally, with changes in Antarctic penguin diets observed via satellite imagery [152], and World War I ammunition depots being exposed by melting glaciers in Italy's Dolomites [161]. The European Union (EU) is promoting measures to mandate member states to develop plans to prepare for a 3-degree Celsius rise in global warming, thereby raising awareness of the severity [140].

sections.title: ⚠️ Climate Inequality and the Issue of Shirking Responsibility
sections.content: The climate crisis is exacerbating social inequality, and criticism regarding accountability is growing louder. According to an Oxfam report, one super-rich individual's impact on heatwaves is 400 times greater than that of an ordinary person. The report also points out that the top 0.1% of the world's ultra-wealthy emit more carbon than 3.5 billion people, thereby fueling the climate crisis and reaping immense profits [11, 34, 151]. Shocking research findings have also been released, indicating that these individuals are gaining a 'double benefit' from both causing and bearing the costs of the climate crisis [139, 162]. Warnings that over 200 million people could become climate migrants if climate change is not adequately addressed raise serious concerns for the future of humanity [12]. Domestically, some public institutions, while advocating for carbon neutrality, continue to increase investments in fossil fuels, leading to criticism about a significant gap between climate goals and reality [48, 59]. Despite climate change being perceived as a cost burden [2], there is a phenomenon where the climate crisis is acknowledged, but climate responsibility is shirked [18].

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts Towards Carbon Neutrality Transition and Climate Adaptation
sections.content: Multifaceted efforts for carbon neutrality transition and climate adaptation are underway both domestically and internationally to address the climate crisis. Jinju City is fully committed to responding in areas directly impacting citizens' lives, such as strengthening tap water management in preparation for climate change and seasonal transitions, and operating a special task force [5, 8, 30, 38]. Ulsan is pursuing various policies, from climate change disclosure to a green grand transition [9], and the Gyeonggi Provincial Council emphasized the need for sustainable school meals in response to the climate crisis [25]. The Jeonnam Gwangju Integrated Special City is leveraging climate tech to accelerate the decarbonization of local industries and achieve carbon neutrality [51, 53, 58, 76, 81, 83, 86], while the Chungnam Provincial Council is exploring carbon neutrality solutions through carbon removal technologies [44, 52]. Furthermore, activities for education and awareness-raising are active: the Gyeongbuk Chilgok Office of Education and Hyosung T&C signed an agreement for climate change awareness promotion and resource circulation education [21], and the Jeonbuk Office of Education and Jeju are spreading carbon neutrality practices in daily life through environmental education festivals [55, 61, 66, 67, 71, 73, 80, 85]. Internationally, global cooperation to address the climate crisis continues, with the European Union (EU) mandating member states to develop climate adaptation plans [27], and the Green Climate Fund (GCF) supporting forest protection in Cameroon [147].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Expansion and Future Power System Establishment
sections.content: As the global transition to renewable energy accelerates, South Korea is also actively working to establish a future power system. With an increase in nuclear power generation, South Korea is seeing a 6% expansion in renewable energy generation, signaling a full-scale shift in its power production structure [96]. Korea Midland Power (KOSPO) is expanding its Virtual Power Plant (VPP) business, linking renewable energy with Energy Storage Systems (ESS), in preparation for a 100 GW era of renewable energy [87, 101, 104, 107]. LG Energy Solution is collaborating with global renewable energy companies to expand its ESS business into Europe and North America [103, 111, 118, 119, 138]. Citizens of Hampyeong County are strongly expressing their commitment to a locally-led renewable energy transition, urging the designation of a national special zone for the creation of an 8 GW renewable energy production base [89, 92, 105, 108, 109, 128, 130, 132]. The Asia Investor Group on Climate Change (AIGCC) has proposed solutions for large-scale power demand, advocating that South Korea's semiconductor and AI mega-projects should be powered by renewable energy [91, 100, 117]. Furthermore, eco-friendly energy technology innovation continues, including the successful domestic first-ever supply of commercial renewable ammonia fuel to ships at Ulsan Port [131]. However, challenges remain, such as the solar inverter's overvoltage response rate being only 3.6% [19], the concentration of the clean energy supply chain, and the projected global decrease in additional clean energy capacity this year [163, 164].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing clearly highlights the severity of the climate crisis and issues of inequality, while also demonstrating the ongoing multifaceted domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition. It is time for all of us to act together to create a sustainable society for future generations, by viewing the challenges and opportunities we face in a balanced way. This concludes today's climate briefing.
